headline: The Defense Department says it has stopped using Anthropic's AI products, and an appeals court has backed its decision to treat the company as a supply chain risk.
score_reason: Follow-up of yesterday's story; the new facts are the on-the-record confirmation and the two court rulings, so one point lower than the pool score.
importance_line: The Pentagon has cut itself off from a leading AI model and Anthropic's legal route is now appeals, but yesterday's BBC account said Claude was still in use last week, so how complete the halt is remains unsettled.
summary: MeriTalk reports that a Pentagon spokesperson confirmed "The Department of War has ceased the use of Anthropic products", eight months after Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth labelled the AI company a supply chain risk when it objected to Claude being used for mass surveillance and fully autonomous weapons; our 6 Oct 2026 edition carried the BBC's report of the halt. New today is the legal picture: the D.C. Circuit upheld the label 2-1 on 25 Sep 2026, so the Pentagon may keep Claude out, while a California judge on 27 Aug 2026 sided with Anthropic against broader federal restrictions, and Anthropic could still ask the full appeals court or the Supreme Court to act.
notes: Read MeriTalk because hstoday.us returned 403; hstoday headline matches. Score 8 to 7 because mostly a follow-up to the 6 Oct entry.
